prompt: Use case identity-preserve. Transparent production spritesheet of ONLY reference canal child: thin long-legged cricket with ivory face dark eyes, huge nacre conical rain hat with red ties, long fine antennae/whiskers, indigo patterned cape and blue shorts, red scarf, backpack with paper boat, bronze flute and bell. Preserve exact handdrawn watercolor ink style, no redesign. 4 columns x4 rows=16 cells, every figure SMALL with entire hat antennae whiskers fingers toes backpack inside inner60% of cell. Huge transparent gutters separating every pose, fixed camera/scale facing right and consistent foot origin. Row1 four idle breathing/blink frames with antennae and hat tassels flexing. Rows2+3 eight consecutive expressive talking frames, free hand opens, points then returns, mouth/head changes and cape follows: real body/limb deformation not translations. Row4 two greet bow/hand wave frames then two quiet resting seated frames. Genuine transparent alpha background, no text/grid/numbers/shadows or background glow, no additional props/characters. Entire character must never touch or overlap another cell. CRITICAL: The last output rows touched. Make a square canvas not wide. Each sprite MUST have only 50% CELL HEIGHT. At least 25% empty transparent space ABOVE head/antennae and BELOW feet per cell. Absolutely no antenna anywhere near another row's feet. Sixteen small isolated sticker figures with very large 50% blank area gutters.

qa.notes: Same costume, props and ink/watercolor identity preserved; 16 complete distinct poses. Per-pose reviewed silhouette bounds with 1px alpha<=24 border, rather than naive equal-grid cuts. Four idle, eight talk, two greet, two rest. Original alpha pixels preserved.
